about: People per place on 1 January 1291 = the place's people of 1356 (public/data/setup_1356.json, after the first wave of the Black Death, 1347-1353) times the factor of its region: the people before the plague over those after it. Between 1291 and 1347 the population of most of Europe was nearly level (England 4.75 M in 1290 and 4.81 M in 1348 after Broadberry et al.; the famine of 1315-1322 in between), so the eve of the plague stands for 1291. The first region whose box holds the place applies; a place in none keeps its number of 1356. Culture, faith and minorities are those of 1356 (a gap).
sources: S. Broadberry, B. M. S. Campbell, A. Klein, M. Overton, B. van Leeuwen, British Economic Growth 1270-1870 (2015), table 1.06: England 4.75 M (1290), 4.81 M (1348), 2.60 M (1351)

A. Izdebski et al., 'Palaeoecological data indicates land-use changes across Europe linked to spatial heterogeneity in mortality during the Black Death pandemic', Nature Ecology & Evolution 6 (2022) 297-306: steep decline in Scandinavia, France, south-western Germany, Greece and central Italy; continuity or growth in much of Central and Eastern Europe, Ireland and Iberia
G. Alfani and T. E. Murphy, 'Plague and Lethal Epidemics in the Pre-Industrial World', Journal of Economic History 77 (2017): Black Death mortality in Europe 35-60 %
M. W. Dols, The Black Death in the Middle East (1977): Egypt and Syria lost about a third of their people
U. Schamiloglu, 'The Golden Horde' and the plague of 1346 in the Qipchaq steppe (in: Pandemic Disease in the Medieval World, 2014)
notes: Factors other than England's are derived, not measured: high-mortality regions 1.65 (a loss of 40 %), middling 1.45 (31 %), low 1.10 (9 %), within the 35-60 % range for Europe and Izdebski's pattern. They are estimates to be replaced by country studies.
Lands the Black Death did not reach in 1347-1353 (sub-Saharan Africa, southern Arabia, India) keep the numbers of 1356.
Cities: the persons of the 30 largest cities are still those of 1356 (src/sim/content/cities_1356.json, a placeholder).
